Thanks Vivek — we reviewed with procurement and legal and they returned a redline. High level: procurement is OK with an escalator but wants a hard cap at 7% and a written true-up that prevents retroactive increases beyond the invoice period. Legal is pushing back on the minimum-floor structure: they want a mechanism that reduces the minimum if usage materially undershoots forecasts in the first 12 months (they called it a "long-tail mitigation").

I've attached their redline: OrderForm_ExhibitD_redline_novum.docx. Key asks from our side:
- Cap annual escalator at 7%
- Add a floor-reduction trigger if monthly utilization is < 50% of committed baseline for 3 consecutive months
- Clarify that any true-up is prospective and limited to a single subsequent billing cycle (no retroactive multi-month clawbacks)

Can your team propose clean language we can consider? We're aiming to keep the commercial economics similar to the initial draft but need these protections for our budget committee.

Best,
Sara Hudson
Senior Procurement Manager, Novum Health

Team, forwarding Novum's redline and procurement asks. Short summary of negotiation posture from the customer: they want predictability (hard cap on escalator) + a contingency to reduce minimums if they underutilize early.

Commercial context: RDW-5691 — $1.2M ACV committed with an initial baseline that assumes a 9-month ramp. If we agree to an aggressive floor reduction trigger we'll lose some minimum dollars but improve likelihood of adoption and expansion. Proposed concession (sales): allow a temporary floor reduction tied to a staged ramp (50% of baseline threshold triggers reduction to 60% of the baseline floor for up to two quarters), and cap the escalator at 7% as they request. We should avoid language that allows retroactive multi-month true-backs; customer wants prospective single-cycle true-ups only.

Questions for legal (Neha):
- Can we accept a temporary lower floor for the first 2 quarters with a defined recapture if utilization rebounds?
- Does capping escalator at 7% materially increase our exposure compared to 5%? (pricing models attached)
- Any recommended redline language for the true-up clause that balances customer ask + our billing ops constraints?

Attaching: ExhibitD_markup_for_negotiation.pdf (internal suggestion language).

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Order form — pricing escalator & minimum-floor redlines

Sara / Marissa / Vivek — thanks for the clear summary. Per review, legal is comfortable with a commercial compromise that preserves Redwood's unit economics while addressing Novum's predictability concerns. Proposed clean language below (we've highlighted the operative terms in the attached PDF):

1) Escalator cap: "Annual price increases under Section 2.3 shall not exceed 7% per contract year; such increases shall be applied prospectively at the start of the following billing cycle."

2) Introductory floor relief: "If Actual Monthly Usage is less than 50% of the Committed Baseline for three (3) consecutive months within the first twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, Customer may request a temporary reduction of the Monthly Minimum to sixty percent (60%) of the then-applicable Monthly Minimum for up to two (2) consecutive billing cycles. Redwood may require a one-time reconciliation (true-up) limited to the immediately following billing cycle to recover any shortfall, provided such reconciliation shall not be applied retroactively beyond the single billing cycle and shall not exceed the aggregate amount of fees that would have been invoiced under the unmodified Monthly Minimum for that single billing cycle."

3) True-up mechanics: "True-ups may only be applied prospectively to the billing period immediately following the period in which the relief was granted. No retroactive clawbacks for multiple prior billing cycles are permitted, and any agreed true-up will not exceed the difference between the reduced minimum and the original minimum for the single reconciliation period."

Operational note: billing can implement the single-cycle true-up, but we should flag to Finance that the temporary reduction will reduce revenue recognition in the short term — recommend Sales document the expected ramp and include in the forecast to control for churn risk.

If Novum accepts the above, we'll prepare a redline to return and propose a DocuSign window for execution. Marissa / Vivek — happy to walk through the suggested wording with the customer on a quick call.

Neha Kapoor
